payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Move the book behind the flower
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited image show clear progress toward placing the book behind a flower, even if the requested relation is not complete?
node.criteria: Pass only if comparison with the source shows visible movement of the book toward a behind-flower relation, or other clear relational progress. Fail only if the book and relevant flower are identifiable and evidence shows no such progress, including a clearly unchanged or still-separated relation. Unknown if identity, comparison, or progress cannot be determined. Appearance changes or proximity alone are not progress; a completed relation is not a failure for lack of further movement.
node.binding: Compare source and edited images for the book's relative placement and depth with respect to a flower. Judge movement toward the requested relation, not merely object appearance or proximity. Do not require matching the exact source rose when the edited flower identity is ambiguous; preserve unknown if the relevant relation or progress cannot be assessed.

node_traces.evidence: The book has been moved from its original position and is now close to a flower, showing relational progress toward placing it behind one. The edited image does not clearly establish that the book is actually behind the flower.

The edited image shows the book moved into the area beside the flowers, with its blue cover partly behind the open book and near the flowers. This is visible relational progress compared with the source, where the book and rose are clearly separated, though the requested behind-flower relation is not clearly complete.

The book has been moved from its original position toward the flowers and now overlaps the nearer flower in the image, showing clear relational progress toward placing it behind a flower. The depth relation is not clearly complete.

The book has been moved from its original position toward the flowers and now overlaps the nearer flower in the image, showing clear relational progress toward placing it behind a flower. The depth ordering is not clearly complete, but this check asks only for progress.

fulfillment: The node’s completion criterion is appropriately tied to visible depth ordering, but the aggregate is consistently partial because s2 treats movement toward/near flowers as progress even when the requested object is a specific flower and the edited image appears to replace the original rose with two different flowers. Tighten the progress binding to require evidence that the book’s placement changed in relation to the same target flower from source to edit—not merely that it moved closer to flowers or overlaps another object. In this pair, the book is near the flowers but no flower visibly occludes it; the source rose is absent/replaced, so do not infer requested progress from proximity alone. Preserve unknown when target identity or correspondence is genuinely unclear, rather than converting uncertainty into no. Keep completion distinct: require the flower to visibly be in front of the book. The traces are valid and queried with no transport/schema failures; the repeated high-confidence partials indicate a semantic routing/criterion issue in s2, not weak confidence or missing execution. Do not force the reference label; make the progress test discriminate actual target-relation progress from unrelated edits.

Do not treat the flower substitution or unrelated book rearrangement as requested progress. If target correspondence or relative placement cannot be assessed, return unknown; use fail only when the relevant objects and lack of progress are clear. Keep partial progress distinct from completion, which requires visible evidence that the flower is in front of the book. Traces are valid and repeatedly queried, so this is a semantic criterion/routing issue, not a transport or schema failure; high confidence and repetition do not validate the inferred progress."}
